entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Orophernes of Cappadocia was a key figure in the tumultuous succession of Ariarathes IV's kingdom in the late 3rd century BCE. Born in Cappadocia, he was one of the two sons Antiochis pretended to have with Ariarathes IV, which led to the legitimation of a child named Mithridates and the eventual deposition of Orophernes' own son Ariarathes V.

This complex web of family politics and succession crises had far-reaching consequences for the region, setting the stage for the rise of the Seleucid Empire and the eventual decline of Cappadocian independence.

Despite his significant impact on the region, Orophernes' legacy has largely been overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, with his name rarely appearing in modern historical accounts of the period.
